title: Reference Mach number
overview: Reference Mach number loaded by NsCom::Init and used to derive the compressible-flow thermodynamic scaling constant const_cp = 1 / ((gama_ref - 1) * mach_ref^2).
principle: Mach number is a nondimensional ratio of flow speed to local speed of sound. Distinguish a local field value from a free-stream/reference input: mach_ref is a reference input, not the local Mach number at every mesh point.
architecture: NsCom::Init reads mach_ref and gama_ref from the runtime parameter database, then computes const_cp = 1 / ((gama_ref - 1) * mach_ref^2). This contract records the initialization expression but does not claim the complete downstream dependency graph of const_cp.

proves: NsCom::Init reads mach_ref and gama_ref as Real values.
NsCom::Init computes const_cp using the square of mach_ref and gama_ref - 1.
The mathematical reference distinguishes local Mach number from free-stream/reference Mach number.
does_not_prove: An admissible numeric range or explicit zero-Mach validation policy.
Physical correctness or accuracy of a particular simulation.

verification.reference: NsCom::Init mach_ref read and const_cp derivation
verification.scope: Source-backed initialization expression; no test execution or independent physical verification is implied.

formulas.title: Speed of sound for a calorically perfect ideal gas
formulas.plain: a^2 = gamma R T,   a = sqrt(gamma R T)
formulas.assumptions: Applies to a calorically perfect ideal gas with constant specific-heat ratio gamma. For a general fluid, a^2 = (partial p / partial rho)_s.

references: Anderson, J. D., Modern Compressible Flow: With Historical Perspective, 3rd ed., McGraw-Hill, 2003, Sections 1.3 and 3.3 (local Mach number and speed of sound).
White, F. M., Fluid Mechanics, 4th ed., McGraw-Hill, 2008, Chapter 9 (compressible flow; Ma = V/a).
NASA Glenn Research Center, Role of the Mach Number: https://www1.grc.nasa.gov/beginners-guide-to-aeronautics/role-of-the-mach-number/
Engineering Handbook, 2nd ed., Chapter 36, The Mach Number and Flow Regimes: https://aghajar.okstate.edu/sites/default/files/pub-pdfs/Compressible%20FLow%20_Chapt%2036%20of%20CRC%20Handbook.pdf
caveats: Notation varies by author and discipline. Record aliases as common usage, not as universal standards.
Local Mach M and free-stream/reference Mach M∞ are related concepts but are not interchangeable in a spatially varying flow.
The ideal-gas sound-speed equation requires its stated thermodynamic assumptions; for real fluids use the isentropic derivative definition.
The source expression is confirmed in codes/ns/src/NsCom.cpp. Its complete physical derivation and downstream const_cp consumers remain to be audited.
